name: Small Intestine: Obstruction, Crohn Disease, Meckel Diverticulum, and Mesenteric Ischemia

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / World Society of Emergency Surgery
clinicalPearls: Postoperative adhesions represent the most common cause of mechanical small bowel obstruction in developed countries
Closed-loop obstruction and small bowel volvulus carry imminent risk of strangulation and require emergency surgical exploration
Gallstone ileus produces Rigler triad on plain radiograph or CT: pneumobilia, small bowel obstruction, and an ectopic radiopaque gallstone
Surgical management of Crohn disease is bowel-sparing: stricturoplasty (Heineke-Mikulicz) is preferred over extensive resection to prevent short bowel syndrome
Meckel diverticulum represents persistent vitelline duct remnant with rule of 2s: 2% prevalence, 2 inches long, 2 feet from ileocecal valve, and ectopic gastric mucosa
reference.pathophysiology: Intraluminal bowel obstruction leads to proximal dilation, fluid and electrolyte sequestration, and increased intraluminal pressure. When wall tension exceeds capillary perfusion pressure, mucosal ischemia, bacterial translocation, mural infarction, and perforation ensue. In Crohn disease, transmural granulomatous inflammation leads to fibrotic luminal narrowing, enteroenteric or enterocutaneous fistulization, and intra-abdominal phlegmons. Acute mesenteric arterial embolism causes sudden cessation of blood flow to the SMA territory, producing severe pain out of proportion to physical findings.
additionalDifferentials: Simple adhesive small bowel obstruction versus closed-loop strangulated bowel obstruction
Acute mesenteric ischemia versus acute pancreatitis or ruptured aortic aneurysm
Bleeding Meckel diverticulum in children versus juvenile polyps or intussusception
Gallstone ileus versus recurrent malignant mechanical intestinal obstruction
additionalInvestigations: Abdominal and pelvic CT with intravenous contrast to identify transition point, closed loop, and pneumatosis intestinalis
CT angiography of the mesenteric vessels for suspected acute mesenteric arterial embolism
Technetium-99m pertechnetate scintigraphy (Meckel scan) detecting ectopic gastric mucosa in children
Arterial blood gas measuring serum lactate and base deficit as markers of intestinal ischemia
